catalog_quote: [Michels 2017:25] Stress in Lamaholot is not usually contrastive. The general rule is that stress is on the penultimate syllable, but even neighbouring dialects may vary in the details. On Flores we find that the dialects vary in whether they count stress on the word or on the root, and whether schwas can bear stress. For Lewotobi stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word (Nagaya 2011, 79) and the same is true for Lewoingu, but schwas cannot bear stress there (Nishiyama and Kelen 2007, 11). ... Rather less is known about stress in most dialects outside of Flores. Kroon (2016, 52) reports a stress pattern on Solor similar to that of Lewoingu, with penultimate word stress avoiding schwas. I can confirm this pattern for both Pamakayo on Solor and Horowura on Adonara. Stress patterns can sometimes be obscured by sentence intonation. Especially in Pamakayo a strong emphasis on the…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim at the stated place (Michels 2017 sec. 2.2.1 p.25) in the PDF we hold/txt; the supporting Kroon 2016 p.52 passage is also verified in the local lama1277 cache. sources.quote: Areal generalization only: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables' and 'In the languages on Flores, schwa /ə/ tends to have very light syllabic weight, be very short in duration, and tends not to be stress bearing.' No Adonara-specific stress statement.
sources.locator: sec. 3.2.1 'Flores phonology', pp.114-115; Adonara Lamaholot [adr] classified p.165-166 under Nuclear West Lamaholot > Adonara-Ile Ape Lamaholot

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. PhD Leiden (LOT 544). Utrecht: LOT. 595 pp.
sources.quote: 'In Central Lembata, the penultimate syllable of the word is stressed, unless the pen[ultimate] ... Schwa is the only penultimate vowel that cannot be stressed. Words with penultimate schwa are stressed at the ultimate syllable, such as /bə.ˈka/' — a different languoid (Central Lembata), same schwa-avoiding penult pattern; nothing on Adonara.
sources.locator: sec. 3.2.5 'Stress', p.49-50 (Central Lembata grammar); sec. 3.8 p.≈128

sources.quote: No explicit stress rule. Transcriptions p.31: tai [tai] ~ taĩ [`taĩ]; laka [`laka] 'step' ~ lakaN [`lakã]; lodo [`lodo] 'descend' ~ lodoN [`lodõ]; tange [`taŋə] 'attach' — stress mark on the penult of CVCV words, consistent with penultimate stress.
